[1/3] ADR-005 and evaluator core: Interpreter(out=None, args=None) seeds global 'args' list of strings (defaults to []), friendly fix when attempting to call args(), failing-first evaluator tests; [2/3] CLI and runner integration: parse arguments after FILE, -e SOURCE, stdin -, and -- option terminator, passing string args to Interpreter; update test_cli.py with failing-first CLI argument tests; [3/3] demo script in examples/, test_hardening corpora check, README updates, regenerated codebase map, full aikit check pebble, delivery

impact_assessment.why: Pebble scripts currently cannot access command-line arguments, limiting automation and scripting utility; adding script arguments via a global 'args' string list provides idiomatic CLI parameterization while keeping the language surface minimal and dependency-free
impact_assessment.benefits: Scripts can read arguments via 'args[0]', 'len(args)', slices, and for-in loops; CLI runner supports passing arguments after script path, -e code, and via stdin or '--' option delimiter; preserves the three-line positioned error contract
impact_assessment.risks: contract: language surface and CLI option parsing change, requiring ADR-005; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: none, single-threaded execution; state: no persistent state
impact_assessment.mitigation: ADR-005 recorded before code; backward-compatible Interpreter signature; failing-first tests per milestone; 100% test pass and full aikit check pebble gate before each commit

[1/3] Add failing-first regression tests and a finite-float result guard so no arithmetic can produce inf or nan; update the two builtin guards that built non-finite values through arithmetic; pin loop-variable scoping and record ADR-006/007. [2/3] Update README and regenerate the codebase map. [3/3] Run the full pebble test suite and aikit check, then complete the task.

impact_assessment.why: The analysis found that float arithmetic can produce inf and nan (for example float(10 ^ 308) * 10), values Pebble cannot spell in source, and that loop variables leaking into the enclosing scope is unpinned and undocumented.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every user-reachable float stays finite, matching the existing float-literal, float() and int()/floor() contracts; loop scoping becomes a tested contract rather than an accidental side effect.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: arithmetic overflow now raises a positioned EvalError and loops keep their documented non-scoping; dependency: none, standard-library math only; concurrency: none, single-threaded interpreter; state: no files or schemas change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, remainder and power overflow; direct-call tests keep the defensive int()/floor() non-finite guards covered; ADRs and tests pin loop scoping before README updates; full aikit check pebble before any delivery.

[1/3] Failing-first tests and a safe range-length computation: huge bounds must be a positioned range-cap EvalError instead of a host OverflowError. [2/3] Record ADR-008 and verify the codebase map. [3/3] Run the full pebble suite and aikit check, then complete the task.

impact_assessment.why: range(start, stop, step) computes len(range(...)) before applying its cap; with a huge but legal int bound Python raises OverflowError, so the CLI reports an internal error instead of the documented positioned What/Why/Fix error (ADR-003, ADR-001).
impact_assessment.benefits: Every range is capped before allocation and huge bounds produce the same explanatory EvalError as other oversized ranges, so no user program reaches the internal-error path.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the range cap is computed with integer arithmetic instead of len(); dependency: none, standard library only; concurrency: none, single-threaded interpreter; state: no files or schemas change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for huge positive, stepped and negative ranges, a formatted-error corpus entry, and the full aikit check pebble gate.

[1/3] Add failing-first tests for a non-finite float argument to float() and for sequence concatenation over the cap, then guard both. [2/3] Record ADR-009, update README and the codebase map. [3/3] Run the full pebble suite and aikit check, then complete the task.

impact_assessment.why: The analysis found two residual contract gaps: float() returns an already non-finite float unchanged even though ADR-004 says non-finite results are refused, and string/list + bypasses MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH so concatenation can grow without bound while repetition and ranges are capped.
impact_assessment.benefits: The conversion builtins share one non-finite contract for embedders, and every user-visible sequence constructor now respects the same 1,000,000-value memory bound.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: string/list concatenation over the cap now raises a positioned EvalError and float(inf/nan) is refused; dependency: none, standard library math only; concurrency: none, single-threaded interpreter; state: no files or schemas change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for both guards, a patched-cap test that stays fast, direct-call coverage for inf/-inf/nan, ADR-009, README/map sync, and the full aikit check pebble gate.
